Hal tara min futur (do you see any fissure): i.e., any crack or breach.

Karratayn (twice): i.e., twice, one time after another.

Khasi'an wa huwa hasir (humbled while he is fatigued): i.e., humiliated and driven away, exhausted, weary, its sight cut off, since it sees no flaw.

**لو كنا نسمع أو نعقل** (If only we had listened or reasoned): that is, they reproach themselves, saying: if we had been listening or reasoning in the world, we would have believed and worshipped Allah, and we would not be today among the companions of the blaze.

When Allah mentioned in the previous verses that He has prepared for the devils, who eavesdrop from the angels in the heaven, the punishment of the Blaze, He followed it with His saying ﴿And for those who disbelieve in their Lord is the punishment of Hell, and wretched is the destination﴾. That is, those who denied His divinity and His meeting, and did not worship Him nor believe in Him, among mankind and jinn, will have the punishment of Jahannam. It is the destination to which they will return and at whose punishment they will end. Its drink is boiling water, its food is thorny plants and zaqqum. And His saying, describing what happens in the Fire: ﴿When they are cast into it, they will hear from it a roaring while it boils﴾. When the disbelievers are cast into the Fire, they will hear from it a roaring, that is, a loud, frightening sound like the braying of a donkey when it brays or neighs. ﴿While it boils﴾, that is, seethes, ﴿almost bursting with fury﴾, that is, nearly splitting apart from the rage which is the intensity of anger. Every believer who knows Allah becomes angry at what angers his Lord and is pleased with what pleases his Lord. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 67, verses 16–19:

Explanation of the words:

"An yakhsifa bikum al-ard" (that He cause the earth to swallow you): i.e., He makes it such that you sink into it and find yourselves within its depths.

"Fa-idha hiya tamur" (then behold, it shakes): i.e., it moves and convulses until the swallowing of you is complete.

"An yursila 'alaykum hasiban" (that He send upon you a violent wind): i.e., a fierce wind that pelts you with pebbles so that you perish.

"Kayfa nadhir" (how was My warning): i.e., what was the outcome of My warning you of the punishment through the tongues of My messengers.

"Fa-kayfa kana nakir" (how was My rejection): i.e., My rejection of their disbelief, denial, and rebuttal was a true rejection, falling exactly where it belonged.

"Saffat" (spreading out): i.e., spreading their wings.

"Wa yaqbidna" (and folding): i.e., and holding their wings in.

"Ma yumsikuhunna illa al-Rahman" (none holds them up except the All-Merciful): i.e., so that they do not fall to the ground, whether when spreading their wings or when folding them.

Meaning of the verses:

He, the Exalted, admonishes His servants so that they believe in Him, worship Him alone, and thus attain perfection and happiness: "Do you feel safe from He who is in the heaven?" That is, the Absolutely Exalted, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in His loftiness above His Throne, distinct from His creation, that He would cause the earth to swallow you, so that you all perish within it. "Then behold, it shakes" at the time of the swallowing, moving and convulsing until you sink into its belly. The answer is that they did not feel safe from this, so how then do they persist in polytheism and in denying the Messenger? His saying "Do you feel safe from He who is in the heaven" refers to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: that He would send upon you a violent wind carrying pebbles and stones, destroying them. "Then you will know how My warning was": that is, My warning you of disbelief and denial, that it is true and that its consequence is realized.

His saying, Exalted is He: "And those before them denied, so how was My rejection?" such as 'Ad and Thamud and others. That is, they denied My messengers after they had been rebuked for polytheism and disbelief, so We destroyed them. "How was My rejection?" That is, My rejection of them was true and its consequence realized.

His saying, Exalted is He: "Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading and folding their wings?" That is, spreading their wings and folding them; none holds them in their state of spreading or folding except the All-Merciful, whom the polytheists denied, saying, "And what is the All-Merciful?" while they live within His mercy, which encompasses everything, and it is manifest even in the birds, which He protects from falling and being crushed. That is, do they deny the divinity of Allah and His mercy, when they have not seen the birds, spreading and folding their wings, and none holds them but a human? Then who holds them? It is the All-Merciful, may His majesty be exalted and His dominion be great, by whatever laws and ordinances He wills, by which He governs His creation and manages His dominion. Indeed, the affair of the polytheists in their disbelief in Allah is astonishing. His saying: "Indeed He is All-Seeing of everything": the one swimming in water, the one roaming the earth, the bird in the sky, and the one hidden in the wombs are all alike to Him.

Guidance from the verses:

1- A warning to those who turn away from Allah, and a warning of the evil consequences should they persist in their aversion, for Allah is able to cause the earth to swallow them or send upon them a violent wind from the sky, and there is no one who can grant them security or protection in any circumstance, except their faith and submission to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

2- In the earlier destroyed peoples there are lessons and admonitions for whoever has a living heart and a mind with which to reason.

3- Among the signs of Allah in the horizons that point to His power, knowledge, and mercy, which necessitate worshipping Him alone, is the flight of birds in the sky as they spread and fold their wings. They do not fall: by supposition, they should keep flapping their wings, pushing themselves to fly with the help of the air; were they to fold or spread them without that, they would be expected to fall, but the All-Merciful, Mighty and Majestic, holds them up so they do not fall.

"Then behold, it shakes" at the time of the swallowing, moving and convulsing until you sink into its belly. The answer is that they did not feel safe from this, so how then do they persist in polytheism and in denying the Messenger? His saying "Do you feel safe from He who is in the heaven" refers to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: that He would send upon you a violent wind carrying pebbles and stones, destroying them. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 67, verses 28–30:

Explanation of the words:

"Qul ara'aytum" (Say: Have you considered?): i.e., tell me.

"Wa man ma'iya" (and those with me): i.e., the believers.

"Aw rahimana" (or has He shown us mercy): i.e., He has not destroyed us.

"Fa-man yujir al-kafirin" (then who will protect the disbelievers): i.e., then who will safeguard and shield the disbelievers from the punishment?

"Qul huwa al-Rahman" (Say: He is the Most Merciful): i.e., say: He is the Most Merciful, the One to whom I invite you to worship.

"In asbaha ma'ukum ghawran" (If your water becomes sunk into the earth): i.e., sunken, out of reach of buckets and not seen by eyes.

"Bi-ma'in ma'in" (with flowing water): i.e., water that eyes can see because it flows upon the earth.

Explanation of the verses:

The noble context continues on the subject of guiding the disbelievers of Quraysh. Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger: Say to these polytheists, who wished for your death and said, "We await for him the misfortunes of time" [Qur'an 52:30], say to them: ﴿Have you considered?﴾ i.e., tell me ﴿if Allah destroys me and those with me﴾ from the believers, ﴿or has mercy upon us﴾ so that He does not destroy us with punishment, ﴿then who will protect the disbelievers from painful punishment?﴾ The answer: no one. So what benefit do you gain from our destruction? As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: He is the Most Merciful. We have believed in Him, and upon Him we have relied﴾, i.e., say, O our Messenger, to these polytheists: Say, He is the Most Merciful, who invites you to worship Him alone and to abandon the worship of others: "We have believed in Him, and upon Him we have relied," i.e., we have depended upon Him and entrusted our affair to Him. ﴿So you will soon know who is in clear error.﴾ And His saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered? If your water should become sunken, then who will bring you flowing water?﴾ i.e., sunken, to say to these polytheists, O our Messenger, as a reminder to them: Tell me, if the water you drink from, "the well of Zamzam" and others, becomes sunken, out of reach of buckets and not seen by eyes, who then will bring you flowing water other than Allah the Exalted? The answer: no one. So why do you not believe in Him, make Him alone in worship, and draw near to Him through the acts of worship which He prescribed for His servants to worship Him by?

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification of the enmity the polytheists held toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to the extent that they wished for his death.

2- The obligation of relying upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, after faith.

3- The legitimacy of argumentation to establish the truth and nullify falsehood.

"Fa-man yujir al-kafirin" (then who will protect the disbelievers): i.e., then who will safeguard and shield the disbelievers from the punishment?

"Qul huwa al-Rahman" (Say: He is the Most Merciful): i.e., say: He is the Most Merciful, the One to whom I invite you to worship.

"In asbaha ma'ukum ghawran" (If your water becomes sunk into the earth): i.e., sunken, out of reach of buckets and not seen by eyes.

"Bi-ma'in ma'in" (with flowing water): i.e., water that eyes can see because it flows upon the earth.

Explanation of the verses:

The noble context continues on the subject of guiding the disbelievers of Quraysh. Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger: Say to these polytheists, who wished for your death and said, "We await for him the misfortunes of time" [Qur'an 52:30], say to them: ﴿Have you considered?﴾ i.e., tell me ﴿if Allah destroys me and those with me﴾ from the believers, ﴿or has mercy upon us﴾ so that He does not destroy us with punishment, ﴿then who will protect the disbelievers from painful punishment?﴾ The answer: no one. So what benefit do you gain from our destruction? As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: He is the Most Merciful. We have believed in Him, and upon Him we have relied﴾, i.e., say, O our Messenger, to these polytheists: Say, He is the Most Merciful, who invites you to worship Him alone and to abandon the worship of others: "We have believed in Him, and upon Him we have relied," i.e., we have depended upon Him and entrusted our affair to Him. ﴿So you will soon know who is in clear error.﴾ And His saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered? If your water should become sunken, then who will bring you flowing water?﴾ i.e., sunken, to say to these polytheists, O our Messenger, as a reminder to them: Tell me, if the water you drink from, "the well of Zamzam" and others, becomes sunken, out of reach of buckets and not seen by eyes, who then will bring you flowing water other than Allah the Exalted? The answer: no one. So why do you not believe in Him, make Him alone in worship, and draw near to Him through the acts of worship which He prescribed for His servants to worship Him by?

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification of the enmity the polytheists held toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to the extent that they wished for his death.

2- The obligation of relying upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, after faith.

3- The legitimacy of argumentation to establish the truth and nullify falsehood.
